note: The owner's real programs (tests/fixtures/nc/owner-public) whose program map gEdit gets wrong today.
Read by src/lib/core/profiles/outline.test.ts. A program listed here has no outline golden, because
a golden would record the wrong map as the right one. Instead 'profile' and 'tools' say what the map
has to show — the profile it opens with and every tool change as [line, tool] — and the test runs
that as an expected failure: the day the map is right, the test fails and the entry is replaced by
a golden (npx vitest run outline -u). 'why' is the reason, in the words of tests/fixtures/README.md.
A milling tool change is the M6 block, with the T word of that block or the last one before it.
'ownerReviewed' stays false until the owner has read these answers (plan §9.2).

nc/owner-public/okuma-osp/2.5D_MILLING.m.why: An Okuma milling program read with the turning profile, whose tool rule wants a four- or six-digit T word: T1 M6 is no tool change there.

nc/owner-public/sinumerik/2.5D_Milling.m.why: Opens as Sinumerik, the turning profile until a milling one exists (R2), where every T word is a tool change: the preselected next tool (T2 after T1 D1 and M6) is listed as one too.

nc/owner-public/sinumerik/DRILLING.mpf.why: Opens as Sinumerik, whose turning tool rule makes every T word a tool change: each preselected next tool is listed as a change of its own, so the map shows nine tool segments for five tools and each drilling operation sits under the next tool.

nc/owner-public/sinumerik/Demo_1.mpf.why: Opens as Fanuc (ISO) mill (a detection gap), which reads the tool name of T="…" as no tool number.
